column1: # Curated OCR corrections for Suhrawardy, "The Sayings of Muhammad" (1905).
# Only entries with exactly one plausible reading belong here. Two systematic
# defects account for most of them:
#   * the scan reads the acute accent of the transliteration as an "i"
#   * it confuses e with c (doeth -> docth, each -> cach, seek -> seck)
# Anything ambiguous is deliberately absent, so that qa.py keeps reporting it
# Format: wrong<TAB>right   Matching is whole-word and case-sensitive.
# -- transliteration: acute accent misread as i ------------------------------
# The three -eth forms at the end of this block lived in the corpus unreported
# for as long as qa.py waved through any token ending in -eth without a
# dictionary check. `cateth` is the one that survived even the fix: it derives
# to `cats`, a real word, so only reading the text finds it.
# Found by comparing the two OCR passes over the scan (tools/abbyy_diff.py),
# each read off the page image before being entered here. Where the two passes
# disagreed the image decided: 318 is "her to", not ABBYY's "hereto", and 291
# Heading manglings. Applied to heading lines by the parser as well as to the
# body text, so that a topic lost to the OCR comes back as data.
